thread:
svc_incident_bot: Paging: prefix-cache hit-rate drop >35% in eu-west-1 (affecting 18% of requests) — severity P1. Auto-create incident channel if not already.

jamal (oncall): seeing the alert. grabbing context and paging eng-sre.

maria (eng-sre): I'm on it — looking at prefix cache metrics now. timeline?

jamal (oncall): last good window ~2026-03-15T09:05Z, spike started ~2026-03-15T09:16Z. Customer reports increased latency and some 5xxs.

alex (eng-runtime): forwarding logs from edge nodes — initial glance shows a lot of cache misses for common prefixes. pushing logs to the channel.

ops-analyst: attaching hit-rate timeseries and percentiles (short).

svc_incident_bot: Log bundle uploaded: s3://ri-incidents/2274509123/logs.tar.gz

maria (eng-sre): quick triage checklist: 1) confirm invalidation/eviction event 2) check KV reuse/rehydration 3) check rollout config for cache flush 4) assess customer impact windows.

cheng (eng-ml): hypothesis: recent rollout toggled async-prefetch off, causing high cold-start for cached KV shards. saw a config change at 09:14Z in deploy logs.

alex (eng-runtime): i can confirm a deploy at 09:13:58Z with flag "cache.prefetch.enabled = false" rolled to eu-west. that would drop background rehydration.

jamal (oncall): @alex can you revert or patch a canary to re-enable prefetch? We need mitigation ASAP if that's the root cause.

alex (eng-runtime): spinning a patch now — will flip flag on 2 nodes as canary.

maria (eng-sre): while patching, can folks dump prefix eviction counts and KV rewarm logs? share the grep snippets here.

alex (eng-runtime): paste logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:14:02Z] CONFIG_ROLLOUT: rollout id=ab12c flag cache.prefetch.enabled=false stage=eu-west
[2026-03-15T09:16:11Z] CACHE_EVICT: prefix=/model/llama/512/ key_count=12487 node=i-0a3f
[2026-03-15T09:16:12Z] KV_REUSE_MISS: shard=27 keys_rehydrated=0 node=i-0a3f
[2026-03-15T09:16:13Z] CACHE_MISS_SURGE: prefix=/model/llama/512/ rps=420 -> 1280
```

cheng (eng-ml): those KV_REUSE_MISS lines look telling — if rehydration stopped, hot prefixes will miss and then cause thundering rehydrates.

ops-analyst: attached hit-rate timeline: 09:05-09:13 stable ~92% hit, 09:14-09:18 drop to 46%, then partial recovery starting 09:29 after canary.

lina (customer-success): one enterprise customer reported degraded embeddings generation between 09:16-09:36; ticket #C-1198 opened. passing along.

jamal (oncall): mitigation in progress: alex reports canary nodes flipped flag back at 09:28Z. monitoring now.

svc_incident_bot: Automated note: rolling revert applied to 20% of e-west nodes at 09:28:34Z.

maria (eng-sre): need to build concise timeline for RCA. I'll start a timeline block here — please paste observed artifacts with timestamps.

--- TIMELINE START ---
09:13:58Z deploy: config change cache.prefetch.enabled=false started rollout (alex)
09:14:02Z rollout event logged (alex)
09:16:11Z first observed CACHE_EVICT and KV_REUSE_MISS spikes (alex logs)
09:16-09:25Z hit-rate falls from ~92% -> ~46% (ops-analyst metrics)
09:20Z customers begin opening tickets for latency/5xxs (lina)
09:28:34Z partial revert applied (svc_incident_bot)
09:29-09:40Z hit-rate begins to recover, tail latency improves (ops-analyst)
--- TIMELINE END ---

maria (eng-sre): hypothesis A: rollout toggled prefetch off causing immediate cold cache and failure to reuse KV; cascade of rehydrates overloaded IO -> evictions and further misses.

maria (eng-sre): Hypothesis B (less likely): a simultaneous KV shard GC/compaction coincided with rollout, increasing eviction pressure. need compaction logs to confirm.

alex (eng-runtime): compaction jobs show normal schedule; no overlapping job at 09:14. pushing compaction logs to bundle.

cheng (eng-ml): quick check — are prefixes with highest misses correlated with large-key workloads (embeddings) or chat? ops-analyst can you slice by route?

ops-analyst: slice shows embeddings generation routes (embed.*) contributed ~60% of the increased miss load during window.

jamal (oncall): customer impact assessment: 18% of requests in eu-west experienced longer tail latency; 2 enterprise customers reported errors (tickets C-1198, C-1199). no data exfiltration.

maria (eng-sre): immediate action items: 1) postmortem owner? 2) gather config rollout audit, prefetch telemetry, KV rewarm logs, compaction schedule, and per-route hitrates. 3) propose a change to rollout gating to avoid toggling prefetch without warmup.

alex (eng-runtime): I can own the revert change and a candidate hotfix for rollout gating.

cheng (eng-ml): I'll correlate model-serving routes and add a regression test for disabling prefetch in staging.

lina (customer-success): I'll coordinate customer comms — summary + mitigation timeline and ETA for RCA.

maria (eng-sre): live notes: recommend follow-up mitigation: 1) require canary with metric gate for cache-hit before global rollout, 2) add graceful drain that keeps rehydration tasks for X minutes during rollout.

jamal (oncall): closing live triage for now; monitoring green. will open RCA thread and assign owners. tagging incident P1 -> postmortem. :white_check_mark:

svc_incident_bot: Incident transitioned to post-incident review state. Log bundle and timeline preserved at s3://ri-incidents/2274509123/ for RCA writeup.

maria (eng-sre): copying final checklist for postmortem: timeline, hypothesis A/B with evidence, action items (owner+ETA), customer impact summary, follow-ups for gating and observability (more granular prefetch metrics).

alex (eng-runtime): adding runbook note: "avoid toggling cache.prefetch.enabled without staged warmup; implement canary metric gate".

cheng (eng-ml): adding evaluation tests to ensure embeddings route warmup within 10 mins if prefetch toggled.

maria (eng-sre): thanks everyone — I'll start the formal RCA doc and ping owners for writeups. closing thread updates here; keep additional logs in the S3 bundle.
